options: Non-technical people, such as management, who do not write code to access data at database level
questions.explanation: Data Surfing is normally done by non-technical people like management who do not know how to write any kind of code to access data at database level.

questions.stem: At what level do Data Surfers normally stay when exploring data?
options: Dashboards and reports, clicking around to explore data
questions.explanation: Data Surfers normally stay at the level of dashboards and reports, where they click here and there to explore data for the information they need.

questions.stem: Which category of tools came into being to cater for the Data Surfers' world?
questions.explanation: BI tools came into being to cater for the Data Surfers' world, where data had to be presented so non-technical people could view it for decision making.

questions.stem: In the Static Reports era, what happened if the business wanted one more column after go-live?
options: The whole development cycle had to restart from scratch
The user dragged the column onto the dashboard
The BI tool added it automatically
The semantic layer exposed it instantly
The report refreshed with the latest data
questions.explanation: In the Static Reports era, dashboards and data were not changeable, so any new column or latest data meant the whole development cycle had to restart from scratch.

questions.stem: What changed in the Dynamic Reports era of Data Surfing?
options: Users could drag and drop tables and columns
Data was directly connected to backend databases, so it was always the latest, although dashboards were still not changeable
questions.explanation: In the second era, BI tools connected data directly to backend databases so front-end data was always the latest, though the dashboards and reports themselves were still not changeable.

questions.stem: What defines the Adhoc Reports era of Data Surfing?
options: Reports were shared in paper format only
Dashboards and reports are changeable, and end users can drag and drop tables and columns
Data had to be requested from IT for every change
Reports were refreshed once a year
Only IT could view the dashboards
questions.explanation: In the latest era, dashboards and reports are also changeable: end users and management can drag and drop tables and columns.

questions.stem: Which requirement did the Adhoc Reports era introduce, improving the Data Surfers' experience?
questions.explanation: The latest era introduced the requirement for a semantic layer, due to which the Data Surfers' experience got better and better.

questions.stem: Web surfing on applications like Twitter, LinkedIn and Facebook is used as an analogy for Data Surfing to make what point?
options: That surfing always changes the underlying data
That surfers must write code to find information
That social media is a form of data warehouse
That surfers only view data to find information, without changing it
That data surfing is limited to mobile devices
questions.explanation: When surfing these applications we do not change any data, we just view it; likewise, in Data Surfing data is ideally not changed but only viewed to extract the information hidden underneath.

questions.stem: Data Surfing is said to be done on which kind of data?
options: Only data older than a year
questions.explanation: Data Surfing is done on data generated by others; it should not be mixed up with data generated by yourself.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the three eras of Data Surfers described?
options: All three of the eras named are correct
questions.explanation: The three eras are Static Reports, Dynamic Reports and Adhoc Reports; Predictive Reports is not one of them.
